title: A Signal for the Orbit
premise: Ulyana Reyes, a xenolinguist whose mind has been rewired by years of translating an extinct alien tongue, pilots the freighter Long Silence along a route of abandoned colonies. A ghost entry on the manifest — a passenger name belonging to a ship that never launched — pulls them into a conspiracy between the two warring human factions, both of whom believe Ulyana unknowingly carries the last intact transmission of the enemy they destroyed. Hunted by a war-crimes tribunal that wants the truth buried and a resistance cell that wants it broadcast, Ulyana must decode the message hidden in their own fractured dreams and choose whether to deliver it. In the end, Ulyana broadcasts the truth to both fleets at once, ending the war at the cost of their identity, their ship, and their ability to speak any language at all.
about_author: Mara Lockridge is the pen name of a former shipping-logistics analyst who spent a decade writing route reports for intercontinental freight before turning to fiction. She lives off-grid on the Atlantic coast, where she claims the fog does most of her plotting for her.

chapters.title: The Long Silence
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Establishes the freight run between dead colonies and Ulyana's condition: they no longer dream in any human language, only in the cadence of the extinct Veth. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as armor.

chapters.title: A Name That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. While reconciling cargo manifests, Ulyana finds a passenger listed on the Meridian Star — a ship that burned on its launchpad nine years ago. The name is Ulyana's own birth name, which no record should contain. Beat: cold dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: Docking at Ashfall
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At the Ashfall station, a dockmaster recognizes the manifest anomaly and quietly warns Ulyana that tribunal auditors are asking about the Meridian Star's cargo. Beat: the safety of invisibility cracking.

chapters.title: The Passenger
chapters.summary: Introduces Sef Okafor, a tribunal investigator posing as a cargo buyer, in his POV. He has traced a forged manifest chain to Ulyana's ship. Beat: professional suspicion shading into fascination.

chapters.title: Dreams in Veth
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana dreams the Veth sequence again — but this time it contains coordinates and a name: Meridian. They wake with a phrase in their mouth they don't remember learning. Beat: uncanny intrusion of purpose.

chapters.title: Audit
chapters.summary: Okafor boards the Long Silence under pretext of inspection. Ulyana's POV as they spar verbally, each testing the other. He finds the forged page; she watches him decide not to log it. Beat: wary mutual recognition.

chapters.title: What the Meridian Carried
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Flashback: the Meridian Star was destroyed to cover up the Veth genocide's final transmission — a confession and a warning, loaded onto a black box that vanished. Beat: guilt as engine.

chapters.title: Run from Ashfall
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Tribunal enforcers arrive to seize the ship. Okafor, breaking protocol, helps Ulyana escape, claiming he needs the black box found before they do. Beat: flight, and the first true alliance.

chapters.title: The Route No One Speaks
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. They take the derelict corridor through dead colonies, and Ulyana explains what the Veth language did to their mind — it thinks in obligations, not words. Beat: intimacy through confession.

chapters.title: Signal at Kestrel's Grave
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A derelict colony relay begins broadcasting the same Veth sequence from Ulyana's dreams — someone is pinging the route, looking for them. Beat: being seen at last, terrifyingly.

chapters.title: The Resistance Cell
chapters.summary: Introduce Iyo Vann, resistance courier, in her POV: she sent the signal. Her cell believes the Meridian black box can indict the tribunal's founders. Beat: hope weaponized.

chapters.title: Bargain at the Broken Relay
chapters.summary: Ulyana, Okafor, and Vann meet aboard the Long Silence. Three agendas, one box. Ulyana's POV as they realize the box can only be opened by a mind that reads Veth — theirs. Beat: reluctant centrality.

chapters.title: Okafor's Confession
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. He reveals he signed the Ashfall cover-up as a junior officer; his investigation is penance. Ulyana must decide if a guilty man's loyalty is worth anything. Beat: trust extended as a gamble.

chapters.title: Intercept
chapters.summary: Tribunal frigate corners them at a fuel depot. Vann's POV: a running battle through the depot's ice tunnels; the Long Silence barely escapes, damaged. Beat: the war's reach is total.

chapters.title: Repair and Rupture
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Stranded for repairs, Ulyana and Okafor argue about ends and means: broadcast the truth and reignite the war, or bury it and let the peace of lies hold. Beat: loyalty vs. truth, stated plainly.

chapters.title: The Second Dream
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The Veth dreams sharpen — the black box's message is not a confession but a warning: the tribunal's founders plan to finish the genocide's logic on their own colonists. Beat: the stakes invert.

chapters.title: Vann's Price
chapters.summary: Vann's POV. Her cell orders her to seize the box and Ulyana by force if necessary. She stalls, torn between the cause and the people. Beat: the cost of belonging.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Threnody Dock
chapters.summary: The cell ambushes them. Vann's POV as she turns her weapon on her own comrades to save Ulyana, taking a wound. Beat: loyalty chosen over ideology.

chapters.title: The Box
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. They recover the black box from the Meridian's hidden debris cache. Holding it, Ulyana's Veth dreams go silent for the first time in years. Beat: dread of completion.

chapters.title: Reading the Dead
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana begins the decoding, and the language starts erasing their human memories as it opens — each phrase translated costs them a name, a face. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: What Ulyana Forgets
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. He watches Ulyana lose their mother's name, their homeworld, and records everything they forget so they can be given back. Beat: love as archive.

chapters.title: The Tribunal's Offer
chapters.summary: Tribunal envoy contacts the ship: surrender the box and Ulyana, and the war ends with amnesty for all. Ulyana's POV weighing the lie inside the offer. Beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Vann's Truth
chapters.summary: Vann's POV. She reveals her cell's true plan: not broadcast, but leverage — use the warning to blackmail the founders, perpetuating the cycle. Beat: the resistance mirrors the enemy.

chapters.title: Split Course
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Vann and Okafor each demand the box; Ulyana, half-erased, must choose a third path. They lock the decoding to their own dying memories — it finishes only if they finish. Beat: terrible agency.

chapters.title: The Founders' Fleet
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Scouting confirms the warning: a colony fleet is being rerouted toward a 'quarantine' that is an extermination. Beat: urgency collapses all debate.

chapters.title: Silence Between Stars
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Quiet chapter: Ulyana, having forgotten why they're fighting, asks Okafor to tell them who they were. He reads the archive aloud. Beat: identity as a gift from another.

chapters.title: Vann's Choice
chapters.summary: Vann's POV. She transmits her cell's plans to Ulyana, burning her own cause, and joins them. Beat: treason as the highest loyalty.

chapters.title: Chase to the Relay Crown
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The final broadcast must be sent from the ancient Veth relay array at the system's edge. Tribunal ships, the founders' fleet, and the remnant cell all converge. Beat: everything in motion.

chapters.title: Boarding the Long Silence
chapters.summary: Tribunal marines board. Okafor's POV: he surrenders himself as decoy, confessing his crimes on open channels to buy Ulyana time. Beat: penance completed in public.

chapters.title: The Last Phrase
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At the relay crown, the final translation requires the last of their human language. Ulyana begins speaking the warning in Veth, and their English, their name, begins to dissolve. Beat: sacrifice at the threshold.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, fragmenting. The message goes out to both fleets: the confession, the warning, the founders' plan, in a language every human mind can feel even if it cannot read. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: The Fleets Halt
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, brief: an envoy, a founder, a colonist mother — the broadcast lands, the extermination order is refused by its own captains. Beat: the war ends not with victory but with shame.

chapters.title: Okafor's Tribunal
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. He turns himself in, testifying with the broadcast as evidence. Justice outside the law becomes justice through it, imperfectly. Beat: accountability accepted.

chapters.title: The Woman Without Words
chapters.summary: Vann's POV. She finds Ulyana alive but aphasic — the Veth took everything. Ulyana recognizes no one. Beat: grief for a living person.

chapters.title: Relearning
chapters.summary: Vann's POV. Months later, on a rebuilt colony, Vann teaches Ulyana human words again, one at a time, using Okafor's archive. Beat: slow, patient repair.

chapters.title: The First Dream in English
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, simple language. Ulyana dreams, for the first time in nine years, in a human tongue. Beat: quiet wonder.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana testifies at the founders' trial, speaking haltingly, and the court listens to every word twice as hard. Beat: voice reclaimed.

chapters.title: A New Manifest
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A new ship, a new route between worlds that are learning to speak again. Vann signs on as crew. Beat: continuation without erasure.

chapters.title: What the Signal Cost
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV, from a tribunal prison. He receives a letter from Ulyana — clumsy, misspelled, alive. Beat: grace across a wall.

chapters.title: A Signal for the Orbit
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Closing image: the old Veth relay array still orbits the dead system, and Ulyana sends one word back to it in thanks — the first word they relearned. Beat: peace earned, memory kept.
